Subject: High p95/p99 latency and increased 500s on /v1/generate (Batch ingestion)

Hi Vanessa,

We're seeing a sharp increase in p95 and p99 latency on the hosted /v1/generate endpoint starting ~08:45 PDT this morning. Throughput for our nightly batch ingestion has dropped ~40% and we're also seeing intermittent 500 responses (roughly 2-3% of calls). This is impacting our downstream pipelines that run hourly.

Attached is a short sample of request IDs and timestamps. Can Redwood confirm whether this is an incident on the Hosted API side or if there's anything else we should change on our end? Our SREs have ruled out obvious client-side spikes.

We need a quick mitigation plan; this is customer-impacting for us.

Thanks,
James Browne

Subject: Re: High p95/p99 latency and increased 500s on /v1/generate (Batch ingestion)

Acknowledged — triage in progress. Initial findings:
- We observed elevated queue length in the request router starting 08:40 PDT correlated with increased tail latency.
- Error rate spike corresponds to saturated GPU workers on a small subset of nodes (model variant: gptx-13b-q4f).
- No recent deploys flagged in last 24h on hosted control plane.

Immediate mitigations applied (08:32-09:20):
1) Auto-scale policy forced additional capacity for hosted tier used by ACME (provisioned +12 worker replicas).
2) Hot-rollback: traffic routed away from the gptx-13b-q4f variant to gptx-13b-q4 (previous quantized variant) for requests over the next 30 minutes.
3) Enabled aggressive KV-cache warmup for the hot routes serving ACME.

We have published a short incident note on status (link below) and are keeping monitoring windows open. Will follow with a postmortem once we have full logs.

Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-02-26-latency

Attaching initial debug snippet for your triage: hostedapi-debug-log-snippet.txt

Ethan Park

Subject: Post-incident update and next steps (INC-2026-02-26-latency)

Hi James — following up with the post-incident summary and next steps. Apologies again for the disruption. Below is a concise rundown; a fuller postmortem draft is attached.

Summary:
- Incident window: 2026-02-26 08:40 - 2026-02-26 09:30 PDT
- Impact: elevated p95/p99 latency and 500s for ~40% throughput reduction during peak batch ingestion; estimated ~2.1% of requests returned 5xx codes during the window. No data loss.
- Root cause (preliminary): a runtime combination of KV-cache miss storm on a hot keyspace + higher-than-expected per-request memory pressure on a small subset of GPU workers running gptx-13b-q4f; this produced head-of-line blocking and queue growth.

Actions taken:
- Immediate routing to stable variant and scale-up (completed 08:32-08:50).
- Hotfixes deployed to reduce per-request memory footprint; longer-term kernel/allocator fix is in flight with ETA 2 weeks.
- Added tighter autoscaling thresholds for affected pools and improved monitoring of KV-cache miss rates.

Customer-facing next steps:
1) We will share a final postmortem by EOW (Monday 03/01) with timeline, RCA, and action items.
2) Laura will follow up on any SLA credit and commercial remediation.
3) We propose a short technical runbook call with ACME SREs to review request patterns and suggested client throttles; available times next week: Tue/Wed 10-12 PDT.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.md (internal draft), hostedapi-debug-log-snippet.txt (truncated), latency_timeline.csv

Please let me know if you want the runbook call scheduled — Laura and I can own scheduling.

Thanks for working through this with us.
Vanessa Ortiz
